2020_05_sep_2020_financial_statement.paragraph: Troy School District's unaudited statements of revenues and expenditures for the period July 1, 2020 through September 30, 2020 were presented in connection with the Board of Education meeting of November 17, 2020, covering the General Fund, the consolidated debt service funds, the consolidated special revenue funds with a schedule for each component fund, and the consolidated capital projects funds. Against an approved 6/16/20 General Fund budget of $151,057,442 in revenues and $161,272,639 in expenditures, first-quarter actuals were $25,704,903 (17.02%) and $16,302,013 (10.11%), so revenues exceeded expenditures by $9,402,890 where the budget anticipated $(10,215,197). No state aid had been recorded, leaving State Sources at 0.00% of the $95,127,294 budgeted.

2020_06_oct_2020_financial_statement.paragraph: Troy School District's unaudited special revenue fund statements for the period July 1, 2020 through October 31, 2020 were prepared for the Board of Education meeting of December 15, 2020, comprising the consolidated schedule for Funds 520, 529, 530, 531 and 535 plus a separate statement for each component fund. Consolidated revenues of $1,785,142 against an approved 6/16/20 budget of $10,925,200 (16.34%) were outrun by expenditures of $1,971,334 against a $10,477,969 budget (18.81%), yielding an actual result of $(186,192) where the budget projected a surplus of $447,231. Federal Sources, at $1,531,252 of $3,268,200, supplied most of the revenue recorded.

Taken together the schedules show federal pandemic-era food and career-technical funding driving nearly all realized revenue in Troy School District's special revenue group during the first four months of the fiscal year, while locally generated revenue in food service, community services, preschool tuition and facility rentals stayed far below the approved 6/16/20 budget levels of 2,198,000, 2,885,000, 2,238,000 and 135,000 respectively. Of the five component funds, only the Community Service Fund reported revenues over expenditures for the period, at 90,057; the Troy Career Center Fund broke even; and Food Service, Troy Preschool and Facilities Rental each reported revenues under expenditures, at (96,997), (144,200) and (35,052).
